rows.title: Choosing Transporter when adding to the address book hands over to adding a transporter
rows.detail: A trader who keeps transporters alongside their addresses needs to add one from the same place they add an address. 'Choose an address type' therefore offers 'Transporter' as well, and choosing it leaves the address form behind and opens the add-a-transporter pages, which start by asking what kind of transporter it is. Nobody has yet decided whether the service manages transporters at all, or whether the address book or something else does, so this waits: the option would otherwise lead nowhere.
acceptanceCriteria: 'Choose an address type' offers the radio 'Transporter' with the hint 'Private, Commercial', listed third, before 'Branch' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-008; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-042; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-110)

On the compose stack and in CDP, choosing 'Transporter' and continuing leaves the address book's add and opens the add-a-transporter page, wherever the real services keep transporter records and their pages; reached that way, that page's 'Back' link returns to 'Choose an address type' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-017; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-048, p16-052; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-148; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-093)
That page shows the caption 'Add a new transporter' and the heading and page title 'Choose a transporter type' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-049; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-148)
That page shows the warning 'Check the transporter list before adding new transporters to avoid duplicates.' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-050)

That page offers the radios 'Private transporter' and 'Commercial', the second with the hint 'This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland.', and a 'Continue' button (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-051, p16-051-m1)

openQuestions: Blocked on transporter management (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p2-031 to p2-037, p2-041, p2-044; c-306): it must be decided whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does. The ruling names nobody to decide it or when, so whoever owns transporter requirements decides, and the transporter area and this row are re-distilled once they have. No safe default: offering the option with nowhere to add a transporter leads nowhere.

Where the add-a-transporter pages live, and which service holds transporter records, follow the real services once transporter management is decided (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-093), so no criterion names a route, a field or a path.
notes: Combines this area's five transporter slices into the one route a trader walks: the Transporter option on the type page (req-1198), the hand-over off the address form (req-1203) and the add-a-transporter type page's caption, warning and radios (req-1204 to req-1206). Building them apart would repeat the same set-up, review and ladder on one journey that is blocked as a whole.

rows.title: Address search opens on the search alone, lists results as the trader types and reveals the fields on a pick
rows.detail: A destination, consignee, importer or branch address is a UK address a trader finds by searching rather than typing out, so those add-details pages open on the address search by itself. Matches appear as the trader types, picking one hides the search and reveals the address and contact fields, an 'Enter address manually' button reveals them for a trader who cannot find the address, and screen readers hear how many results there are and which address was picked. A save with nothing picked or typed reveals the fields as well, so every error summary link reaches a field the trader can see. All of this is script on top of a page that has to work without script, so it waits: the design team has still to say whether the standard address pattern with the fields always visible will do instead, and the address lookup has still to become a real feature of the front door and its backend. If the layout is kept, it is built as an enhancement of the search that already works without script.
acceptanceCriteria: With JavaScript on, 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' open the add-details step with only the address search; the address fields, the contact fields and the 'Address type' uses question stay hidden until an address is picked or manual entry is chosen, and open already revealed when a picked address or address line 1 already has a value (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-025, p16-037; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-083, p16-096, p16-098; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-140, p6-141)

Typing in the address search lists matching addresses below the field in a list labelled 'Address search results', each result showing the name, address and country the lookup gives, with the typed text in bold, and a screen-reader announcement gives the number of results, such as '1 result available' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-027, p16-029, p16-030; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-086, p16-086-m1; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-143; c-178)
Below the address search an 'Enter address manually' link-styled button reveals the address and contact fields (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-036; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-085, p16-130)

Picking a search result hides the address search, reveals the address and contact fields and announces 'Selected <name>' to screen readers (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-033, p16-034; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-087, p16-088)

Saving the search-only layout with nothing picked or typed shows the same six field errors the manual address form shows, from 'Enter a name or organisation name' to 'Enter a phone number', with no message about the search field, and reveals the address and contact fields so each error summary link moves focus to a field the trader can see (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-077; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-092; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-142; repo:insfrontend p3-065; c-180)

After an error, the error messages stay on the revealed fields until the next save, and what was typed, the ticked uses and the search text are kept (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-077; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-094)

With JavaScript off, the page behaves as the search that needs no script does: the address and contact fields are shown and the search button searches on the server (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p1-033, p1-035, p1-086, p1-087; c-305)

Today only the dev-and-local spike exists and no address book page offers a lookup. This area is re-distilled once both land, which also settles when the 'Enter address manually' button shows, because no trace ever shows it revealed.
notes: Combines this area's five address-search script slices into the one increment the 9 October afternoon ruling calls them: the search-only layout (req-1214), results as the trader types (req-1216), the reveal and announcement on a pick (req-2044), the manual-entry button (req-1864) and the errors that reveal hidden fields (req-1285). They share one script, one page and one block, so building them apart would repeat the same set-up, review and ladder.

Combiner: merge into the existing blocked row inc-194 and keep its id, its waiting-on-design theme, its dependsOn (inc-042) and its externalDependsOn on the address-book split workarea (inc-072, inc-081) exactly as they are. The server-side pages the script enhances belong to the split-off address-book branch, so this row reaches them only through those external dependencies and must not list them in touches.

Combiner: merge with the party-address-add-and-edit area's draft for the same row (req-649, req-652 to req-654, req-1957) and the transporters area's draft (req-458, the commercial transporter form's hidden fields), as inc-194 already does, so the search-only layout is built once for the address book, the party pages and the transporter form.

The real lookup supplies the addresses, not a list shipped with the page (c-178 overruled the shipped list), so each result shows the name, address and country the lookup gives: it may give no organisation name, which is why the announcement on a pick names the picked address.
The prototype's error layout, which links an error summary to a field that stays hidden, is a gap and not a design choice (c-180), so the criterion reveals the fields with the errors.

No criterion is split per environment: the row is blocked until the lookup is a real feature in every environment (c-217), so when it builds, every criterion is observable wherever the front door runs.
